content: I began using Quicken in the DOS version.  It has helped me organize all aspects of my financial life.  Ease of use and customizing its capability to suit the way I want and helping to achieve goals in life are outstanding.  It helped to place me in the top 2% of net worth individuals in the U.S.  A godsend.
answered all my questions and were friendly
it is impossible for me to update my current version.  Somehow my computer cannot connect to your server.  Your tech staff cannot resolve this issue.
easy to use, organize, and store years of data
Forced subscription is wrong. Let me just buy the program and use it.
I have been using Quicken for many years and just updated my accounts within minutes this morning. I like it's easy of use and reporting capabilities. Although, I don't like the annual subscription.
Your customer support.  Always there and always so helpful.

I have loved Quicken for more than 35 Years!!!BUT...Recent versions of Quicken do not download from Schwab credit card accounts accurately!! And do not download from Chase investment accounts accurately!! This is becoming painful: please call me at 703-282-5774. Thanks!
Product is completely overpriced
Easy to use;  Reports are many and helps me realize how I am spending my money
Helps me keep organized with both mine and my family's finances
My wife and I like the program but it is way too expensive, the yearly license. We are retired and on a fixed income and I see no reason why the program is as costly as it is.

I've been using Quicken to manage my consulting practice in addition to my personal financial management over the past year and it's great to have it all integrated. Good choice for a business that is uncomplicated, as mine is.
I've been using Quicken for 40 years. There is no better way to manage your finances then Quicken

Great aid fot keeping track of ones finances!  Unfortunately there are bugs in the Quicken program.  After a update I can no longer create Income and  Expense reports and  Quicken support doesn't seem to be able to fix the issue.
We use Quicken and then import into Turbo Tax. I understand that the current tax schedule selections in Quicken match the IRS forms. But I wish there was an option to match Turbo Tax instead.
Ease of use and able to get what I need
Easy to use, like storage in cloud.
I have used Quicken for years and find it really easy to use. I check it daily and it seamlessly uploads all my banking transactions. I would recommend it to anyone
It is a lot more friendly that earlier versions
Easy to use.
When this becomes a cloud solution, it will be worth it
Quicken does everything I need it to do.

I specifically asked if I could use the program without the membership.  Customer service told me yes, that I can only not sync with my bank account.  Not true.  I can't even enter a bill that I had already created.  It's ridiculous, I paid for the program years ago and own it.  I don't need it connecting to anything. Forced into the membership.
It works.  It is very intuitive to use and very forgiving.  My financial world would be impossible to manage without it.

I've been useing Quicken for more than 20 year and I don't think I could live with out it.Quicken is very user friendly and it just keeps getting better each year. The folks at Quicken work hard in keeping up with todays banking needs to keep my Quicken ruuning smooth. I love all the features of quicken as I use most all of them.Thank you Quicken.

Im a long time user of Quicken and appreciate all our finances in one place. Over the years occasional hone support has been very helpful.Lately  several of our accounts in Quicken have to be re-connected to the institute repeatedly. A little frustrating but not anything major.
In my computer is not working well, all the time consider mi like new in the Quicken
I rely on Quicken for planning my monthly budget. Setting up expenses and income is essential. Been using Quicken for over 20 years.
I don't like the new opening screen.  I always have a log out and back in to get to classic.

Quicken is merging different accounts when it shouldn't. You must be using AI or something that is putting transactions into the wrong accounts, ones that aren't even related or at the same financial institution. It often causes several hours of corrections to get the accounts to balance properly. Transactions sometimes disappear and are impossible to trace. Sadly, this software still seems to have most of the features that our household needs and will use it until we can find a better one.
I have been using Quicken for more than 20 years and it never fails.

Ever since Quicken became a subscription to me in March 2023, my program has not performed properly.  I tried tech support and the women who tried to assist was unable to solve the problem.  She said "sorry" and hung up. her foreign accent was not easily understood. I feel tech support is worthless.
I love it all. It is especially helpful for monthly reconciliation of my accounts. I’ve used Quicken since 1988 (as best I remember) so I am faithful. Never even considered a change. Love it!!!
I love quicken it is easy to use, user friendly in every way. For those you are not accountant or blessed with being so good with numbers it takes a step-by-step to take care of business much needed.
Expensive.
I have been using Quicken for Mac since the early 90s.  The best and most important feature is the data integrity.
Have been using Quicken for many years.  Would be lost without it.  Quicken is my mainstay.
I have used Quicken for many years.  It gives me exactly what I need to manage my finances and taxes.  It's been a rock.
They never fixed the ****** in the balance of my manual AE account.
Will not update my Schwab accounts. Keeps showing error. Frustrating.
I can't seem to get my accounts to synch up so they just stay the same instead of showing me latest figures.
The app frequently chooses to not recognize my sign in password. It’s almost as if I have limited sign ins. Very, very frustrating.

I have been using the program for over 20 years and it makes it so easy for me to keep a monthly handle on my finances. I have my own creative way to use the accounts feature for what I call budgeting "buckets" each month, and I don't know what I would do without it!! Keep up the good work improving this wonderful product!

With the update tool, Quicken used to pull info entered into Bank of America bill pay and enter that into the check register. For some reason it quit that update feature and now one must repeat those entries into Quicken for each bill paid.  What happened?
Good budgeting app but option exercise and sales are not calculated correctly.
I've been using Quicken for over 20 years. Love it! You can customize reports anyway you want to see where your money went.
I've been using Quicken for YEARS, and it does everything I need it to do and more.  I can't imagine keeping track of my finances without it.

I have been using Quicken since 1993.  I think it is one of the best personal financial management software on the market.  This software makes it very easy to create budgets, track finances, and establish reports for various categories and events.
I have been using Quicken for many years.  It is easy to use and it helps me keep my accounts in order.
it's very easy to keep track of your expenses.

Have had a lot of issues. One was when I paid the mortgage, it would show I didn't pay it. One problem lost all of my pay breakdowns, taxes etc. My checking account was off by $13,000. Never fixed it.
Many errors and bugs overall, good concept but very good, frustrating to you

Couldn't live without it!I have been using Quicken on my Mac for 30 years or so. I tried using the online version and it seemed too slow, clunky, and the graphic elements were too large. My desktop version has come a long way and I use it every day to track bills. I have automatic entries for months in advance so I can project when I need to transfer funds to pay for something unexpected.  KEEP IT UP!!
Been disappointed that Quicken is now an annual subscription...looking to change products.
Some things in portfolio view never seem to get fixed.  Like day gain and price day change often contradict each other.
Fantastic product to use great customer support
It is still pretty clunky.   The reporting options are lacking...Biggest pain is one step download takes forever and the success report is never complete.
Processing transactions has a long delay and are not appearing in the register as soon as they should.  Check have an unacceptable wait time before sending.
Way too complicated.
Quicken constantly mis-identifies transactions downloaded from my bank. I need to first print my bank actions to determine the correct payee.
The saas version is way more expensive than prior versions.
lt worked, as it should.
Easy to use.  Allows downloads from most financial websites.  I have been using it continuously since 1989

Quicken is the easiest personal financial on the market.  Both windows and Mac.   I have been using it for better than 25 years.  I have tried several others but I keep going back to Quicken. I will also say their tech support is the best in the business.  Hardly any holds longer than 2 or 3 minutes and it’s human.  The have helped me numerous times.
Too many issues with transaction downloads from various sources.  Please fix this because this activity is a primary function of this software application.
Good product, but difficult to maintain data integrity.

There are too many glitches. I'm constantly having to re-enter numbers (e.g. every time I look at Planning and unselect all the travel categories, when I go back in, budgeted amounts revert to something that looks to be based on my actual expenses.I look online for help and everyone seems to be having similar issues.

One step update is not working correctly; double inputs are being discovered when transferring data to Quicken; then when you attempt to delete one of the duplicated files it deletes both files. Quicken has become very unreliable software and I'm switching and have no choice.
The reliability and usefulness of Quicken makes it a joy to work with on a regular basis.
I have used Quicken for years.  It is easy to use and save me a lot of time organizing my files for taxes.  I also love tht my bank and checking accounts are balanced every day.
I had problems combining quicken accounts from 2 bans and the rep spent about 2 hours with me to get it right
Easy to use.  I've done so for over 20 years.
I've been using Quicken since its inception. It's a must for everyone with investments, bank accounts, CDs, etc. Quicken keeps track of all your assets, your budgets, taxes and offers lifetime plans.
I prefer to renew online but in doing so, I dislike my credit card being captured and not being able to remove it, and having automatic renewal selected.

Certain investment overlays have some "bugs" which change entered data and corrective action is ignored. Also, tax reports recharacterize inputs into incorrect categories which make a inputs into TTax impossible. Otherwise, Quicken is the center of our financial house. Thanks since 1993.
I've used Quicken for over 20 years now. I was a little bit surprised on how much of an increase there was for the Cost of the software between 1 year to this year.
Love this app. Been using it 20 years. With the mobile app being synced to my laptop, even more useful. Love being able to manage my debt, and income, even investments.
When I update from Discover card or from my bank I get some bogus data so that I can't reconcile my accounts

I have used Quicken since the mid-1990's and it serves as a complete record of our family's financial activities, and also serves as a source of information on past vacations, places we have been, etc. by looking up stuff with custom date ranges under "Travel," "Dining," "Entertainment," "Kids," and so on. It has a good help file for complex situations and for income taxes, and is also compatible with downloading bank statements to record which transactions have cleared the bank. It was especially useful recently when one of our checks was stolen and used for fraudulent purposes. I used Quicken to document detailed data for our police report.
Easy for the elderly to use.
Reconciled entries, especially credits, "vanish" from accounts and have to be reentered manually.  Very annoying.
Quicken is easy to use and I have tracked my check book for decades.
Using Quicken for many years has allowed me to have all of my financial accounts all in one place! This is extremely helpful to know my status with everything on a page!!
It was very frustrating to get Quicken to recognize that I had changed my default account. I kept getting notices that I hadn't done the change.
So easy to use, constantly updated so I stay current with the software.
I have been using quicken for years. I love that it is easy to use. Knowing my information is backed up and secure is also something I enjoy.

I appreciate the functionality provided in the program, but it seems quite sluggish. I have a pretty fast machine, but the various manipulations in the program always seem to take longer than they should. I would recommend working some on program optimization..
Except for small small errors in handling transactions, does a great job of helping me manage my finances
Product moves slowly.  Seems as if Quicken has become a secondary asset of the company as improvements are marginal.
Over the years, my fidelity downloads via quicken do not match my actual account. Trying to reconcile, but not successful.

Quicken itself works overall fine except the following: When refreshing the total portfolio value, it often asks to login on the Quicken while I am already logged on, and while it supposed to connect to online and to retrieve quotes. Then Quicken practicall hungs up: I cannot proceed any further other than seeing login screen on the Quicken:. This happens even after typing in the correct password, it does not accept the password and  asking the same login request over and over and I cannot proceed the quicken any more. They should fix this serious bug in the program so that Quicken should be a good usable software.
Excellent personal finance software, with great customer service. Can't beat that.

Very useful for home finances but still could use enhancements.  One of the things I use Quicken for is to record events associated with payments: i.e.: auto servicing and miles; vacation events and lodgings, etc.  The memo field could be expanded to allow more detailed histories of such things.
I consider the Customer Support to be first class.
Lower your annual subscription price, $95 is extremely high. I have been a Quicken user for 30 years and I am considering going to a different software because of the cost.

Qicken has failed me twice before, where ALL data was lost.  had to dig through paper records to get 12 months of data back. remaining data years back permanently lost.  Never happened to me before I had a "subscription"
The only "improvement" they've made to this software in 20 years is the annual price increases.

I started using Quicken Simplifi recently and reached out for help on April 14, the day before needing to file my income tax, so my nerves were jangled to start. The representative was so clear and helpful. His calmness and certainty helped me stay calm, so that was a big plus. He guided me through the solution and everything was resolved. Excellent customer service!
It’s a good product that helps me record and track expenses.

The Quicken program is one of the best for handling my finances.  I like to ease to update all my accounts and know my net worth and investment balance in seconds.  I also like how Quicken provides the capability to budget, determine taxes, or manage debt.  I would like that Quicken would provide more tools to manage finances once one enters retirement.

I have used Quicken since '92 and generally have been pleased with it. Recently, while renewing my subscription and installing the "updated" download (the C/S rep was great), there was one challenge after another. It took 1.5 hrs to install. However, now all of the registers have every other line blacked out and so far, nothing works to correct it. It is not user friendly at this time.

Great product for monitoring my finances.Only two wishes:I'd love it to have "rules" I could set up like QB to separate similar transactions. Memorizing transactions doesn't cut it.I'd love an Amazon interface for purchases there.
Makes multiple errors on downloaded transactions. No clear help on how to correct the problem of multiple duplicate accounts created after change with how Chase accounts are handled.

I have in the past sent two email support issues to the support team. In both instances, I never received a response from support. Rather than spend more of my valuable time on it, I simply realize I can’t rely on Quicken Support.  Ultimately, this negative could lead me to find another competitive product.
Easy to use.  Appreciate the changes that were made

Love Quicken’s Customer Service reps. Not only are they real people, but you can actually talk to them AND they know what they are doing. I’ve used Quicken for years….unfortunately I don’t think I’m using it the best way since it has been redesigned. It used to help me be more efficient paying and tracking my bills. Not so anymore. I will say that it’s still awesome tracking things and I’ll continue using it for that reason.

Mac experience continues to lack windows capabilities. Quicken ignores most customer feedback and continues development of features no longer relevant. Meanwhile basic investment total return reports are non-existent, crypto is not supported and options tracking limited. all for a product charging 2x annually what the SW one-time charge used to be.

I like the ability to track expenses, do reports based on my financial information, search for specific expenditures and many other features. My main problem is downloading from my financial information. When it worked at all the downloaded statement did not always match the bank statement. Now I have to download manually instead of the auto method. Last year I spent about half a day with Quicken support and it worked for a few months. The pop up keeps saying do not contact your financial institution, try back later. I'm very close to canceling.
Decent software but expensive.
Always there for banking

I have personal financial data entered in Quicken for over 25 years now.   The searchablilty of the data is very good and is very sticky for me to continue.  The weakness and continued weakness is lack of data analysis tool flexibility.   If I want to do something unique I need to download the dataset and build my analysis in some other software like excel.   This is time consuming and painful.  Just looking for the next level of user defined tools here!
The customer service person listened to my request and was responsive to my needs.
Contacts download is a complete waste.  Data entry is "clunky" and very time-consuming.  Won't be renewing.

This program continues to be very difficult to use. I will discontinue using it as soon as my subscription expires. The company needs to get back to basics and work on simplifying the use of the product. Keep it simple stupid! KISS.
I have Quicken on three devices none of the accounts are the same so I only use one and that account has decided to enter dual expenditures so my balance is a way off and I've had to manually adjust

Gets locked in Sync for hours, rendering it useless till …..   When filing taxes it only listed 3 of 4 checks for property taxes. It doesn’t help build confidence in the reports. Used to be spot on in 1995, what happened?
I appreciate Quicken Classic but don't want to add more "bells and whistles"!
Uploading to Quicken.com destroys my memorized payees.
Easy to use.  Up-to-date and easy to auto-renew.Provides me with everything I need to keep track of all my finances.

Quicken’s computer program is very user friendly and staff is always available to assist you in layman’s terms! The program does an excellent job with helping to manage and keep track your financial portfolio!

Quicken should be a standalone, resident-on-my-computer software. I should NOT have to log in to Quicken via the internet EVER if I don't want to. Updates, patches and bug fixes, sure. But for ordinary use, no. It raises suspicion about what Quicken is actually downloading from me. I don't like it, I don't want it and I should be able to turn it off. The "subscription model" sucks. Cut it out.
One step updates make it easy to keep accounts up to date

Lately something is wrong with the interface with Truist.  When I reconcile (sometimes, not all the time), Quicken is bringing in duplicated records or records that should have pulled into a different account.  This causes me hours of going back in and manually reconciling until I get the correct balance.
For several years Quicken software has helped me keep track of my finances securely and helpfully at a reasonable price
Long time customer.
Have been using Quicken for over 15 years. While not using a lot of the enhanced features, using as a checkbook and budgeting tool has greatly enhanced my ability to manage my finances.
love it. makes calculating my taxes so much easier

Quicken is extremely well planned and laid out so it's very easy to use.  I love the main page which shows a list of your asset and liability accounts down the left side of the page, along with their balances, while the center page shows the transaction register for whatever account you chose from the left side of the page.  Even while Quicken is easy to use, it is very flexible and can record and immense amount of details.  Reports are easy to generate and can be customized a lot to fit your needs.  Quicken downloads all transactions from my financial institutions and reconciles them to my registers for me.  And Quicken transmits all my payments to vendors electronically and seamlessly with my bank.  And Quicken has a lot of other great tools, like the Calendar, Tax Planner, Memorized Payees, Electronic Payees, etc.

I have been using Quicken for decades for tracking home and small business finances.  It is easy to download financial data into Quicken, and for doing taxes it is easy to export data from Quicken into TurboTax.
I've used Quicken for years as a Realtor. The program is user friendly and reports are easy to set up. I don't need all the bells and whistles it offers but it's nice to know it's available.
I have enjoyed using quicken since 1998.  I am happy with the updates.  I am happy that they have a sensitiveTechnical Support.  It is essential!!!
I have been using Quicken for almost 20 years, and have all my financial information in one place. Love it!
Unable to download transactions.  Tried on app and web   Tried on tablet and a computer
Web based downloading was easy. The yearly price is a little steep.
Mostly OK, but often difficult to get input to sync when inputting from 2 locations, and that is frustrating.
I have never seen a software package such as Quicken applies all debits before the credits.  That doesn't or shouldn't be how it should be in my training.Thank you.
I cant remember m;uch about my last encounter with quicken was but I know everytime I get help its wonderful, problem solved  and education on why it occurred.. always happy. thanks
Very expensive now that it is subscription based.  Quick links often needs reaettjng
Solid support and understandable features.
Your expert technicians have never failed to pull me out when I get in trouble.
I always have trouble updating my checking account at PNC. The software does not show the right deduction name, so I must change it manually.

I have the version that lets me do the least, but is perfect and I love it.  Recommend to lots of folks.  I have not had a lot of problems, but when I do, help is there for me and that is the most important thing.
Excellent Customer Service, attention to detail and timely updates.

Always enjoy using this product.  It works well and is quite easy to use if one is familier with the navagation paths one wants to use.  A new user can be overwhelmed by some of the options to navigate.
I need to transfer program to a  laptop  from a desktop and I can't get any information on how to do this.
I love Quicken, but I can’t understand why it doesn’t seamlessly handle Roth Conversions and even IRA withdrawals in retirement. Cmon!
It's a program that helps me keep track pf my finances in one place with many features I frwuently use.

I use quicken on a daily basis.  It provides a quick and easy way to review finances, purchases, and holdings.  Quicken is a fundamental factor in identifying unusual charges and purchases which is a key component for identifying scams and fraud.  Close to real time detection facilitates fast resolution and enhances protection.
System works very well for our needs.  Over the years there have been many improvements to Quicken that I have appreciated.

I use Quicken for our personal/household use.  Sometimes, I will input something (e.g. a charge on a credit card) but, instead of simply adding the total to the balance, for example, but it comes up with a completely different number.  No matter what I do, I can't get it to do what I want.  For example, if I have a balance of five and the next charge is one, it should say the new balance is six.  Instead, it will say 2 or 9 or 15.  No rhyme or reason to any of it.  I end up having to add a "correction" to get the program to agree with the correct totals. Any ideas?

The program keeps telling me every time I start up and try to download transactions from chase I need to update my connection with them, it is irritating and takes me a long time to resolve.  Also the fact that I now have to manually pay bills outside of Quicken is also another big negative, if I knew of an alternative program from Quicken I would probably use it.
Some things are just confusing without clarity on what to do even on simple return
Easy to use, and keep me organized

I have used Quicken to create and generate budget reports for over 20 years. This year quicken is adding lines in the budget I create labeled 'Everything Else". This is unacceptable. I create and control the budget and Quicken should not add anything to a budget that I create.  I reported this last month and again this month and have not heard back. I would like to know when this will be fixed. It is creating unnecessary work for me to edit reports after generating them in Quicken. If you can’t fix this issue can you suggest another finance software I can move to that is more stable?
Why can't Quicken remember categories for repeat payees?

The basic function of downloading transactions from institutions has gotten less and less functional as you add new elaborate functions ... the main purpose for which I use Quicken has gotten less beneficial as the price goes up
Too many glitches, it seems The accounts need resetting far too often.

Your Techs are amazing. I have been using Quicken for a long time. I think you need to reach out to some of the Banking institutions and figure out how to make both of the systems compatible with each other. I have to manually enter transactions from TD Bank. Thanks
Sometimes very buggy.
It does what I need.  Just that simple.
I don't think the value I am receiving from this product justifies the annual fee we all must pay now.

Quicken allows me to easily download and process records from several financial accounts. It also allows me to create several different reports and to customize them to show only the information I want.
Had issues with where the file was located.. Need to have more flexibility or better direction on where to put it

After years of using Quicken I know can no longer reconcile my account. To be honest, I am not an accountant, but I have not had this trouble in the past. I am considering going to Quick books and starting over I am so frustrated.

Bill paying in general continues to have issues.  I have a utility for whom I constantly get "we're waiting for your most recent statement" or some such thing on Quick Pay.  Fortunately, I still get the paper copy, and ultimately just pay from that.I also had credit card bill that I pay with Check Pay.  Earlier this year, my payment didn't get there until a month later than I specified.  Got charged late fees and interest.Both of these are ongoing issues, though that last was exceptionally bad.  I considered going to a lower-service level with Quicken, so I didn't have to pay for bill paying, and just do it through my bank (free).  But, there are enough other features that I'd miss that I decided not to.  At some point, I may just look at moving off Quicken altogether, after over thirty years!

I have been using Quicken for quite a few years, and I am thoroughly happy with the performance of this item. It keeps my banking and investments right at hand so I can see everything at once.  Love it.

Quicken helps me with all my bills and finances. One problem I have is when updating, my program will not show Menards name on purchases on Wells Fargo and Discover cards. I still recommend Quicken to my family.
I have used Quicken since it first came out. Allows me to budget and save effectively.
Overall a useful tool.  Too many quirks that make it very difficult at times to maneuver around
Once things are set up, the system is pretty reliable.
Too expensive.  Account update not reliable.
Bugs never get fixed.  Improvements are minimal, yet I'm still being charged rent on this software.
I ask every year I renew quicken to have Schedule E categories in the drop down list when writing checks and classifying expenses. Every year Quicken ignores my suggestion.

I can not call to help with questions. I have to use the online messaging which is nice but that does not always help and took twice as long to solve. Back when I had help on the phone they were so friendly and help right away because they could understand what was going on.
So easy to use and place images of documents in one place. It's a great product.
Keeps all assets available for review
Have been a user for decades. Always quick and easy to use.
It is so so. I haven't been using it too much because it is not always helpful.
latest update will not install and instructions do not fitas when i try to go to next step it shuts down   not giving me access to options to install

About once a year I get a message that I need to set up the authorization with my bank to allow downloads.   Every time I do this,  and it's always for Citi credit card,  it makes me reset the account which loads it as a new account and it restored ALLtransactions going back years.   I have to manually identify them and remove them.   It also screws up my reconciling.   It is a major undertaking.   Everything else works great,  but this.

quicken slowly improving Mac versionFeatures that were standard in the mid 2000s are finally seeping back into quicken. For a number of years, quicken was quite unappealing but there were few alternatives and switching was time consuming. The U.I. could use improvement but stability is much better.
Difficult to use the budget. Difficult to get help.
difficult to speak with live animalcomputer not very charming
Over charged my account by $1,500Had to spend about  5-6 HOURS on the phone just to TRY to fix itCustomer service is "out of the USA"It's a mess....Beware
Not satisfied when logging back in does not go to latest entries.
We have been using Quicken,  since it 1st came out  so many years ago. Never disappointed us.
My computer crashed and I was unable to get my data because quicken is not cloud base. Absolutely unacceptable.
Let's start with "what went wrong this time".
I was able to make one phone call to get my problem solved, and it was solved immediately.  Great service.
A must have for financial tracking for me for 20years now.
Ideal for maintaining budget, cash flow, spending and tax records.  Been a long-time user and found great value in comparative records over the years.  Great product that keeps improving.

I have had experiences the past few months with two financial institutions that we virtually no help in fixing the problem getting information from investment accounts. Two different gentlemen, who happened to be from Guatemala, stayed with me two help fixed it by identifying the fix to tell the financial institutions.

I've used Quicken since it hit the market. Originally it was great, but after Discover sold the program it seems that with every "upgrade" comes multiple problems. The software agreement continues to increase in price but the customer support is almost none existent. Now I am unable to download transactions from my bank into Quicken?! Will they ever get it right?

I use Quicken Home/Business to do:- register maintenance- downloads- reports (need these for either "where the heck did my money go" or tax/expense reports for my corporation.I do not track stocks or what not.  The biggest issue I have with Quicken is the instability of transaction downloading.  It is the bane of quicken, and sorry, I don't want to hear "it's the banks fault."  I bought quicken from you - just fix it.Technical note: if most of the time resetting the account works, why not just make that a behind the scenes operation?
Difficult to use.  out dated
So user friendly and extremely stable.

I received a renewal notice for Quicken and so I updated my current credit card number. I could not remove the old card due to the limited functionality of the site and no help function. Quicken charged the old card. I emailed for help but did not receive a response. There is only a 650 US phone number and I don't have US calling. I am directed to a public chat page about Quicken Issues when I "contact" Quicken. I pay $100 Cdn a year for this and I can't even get any help. Waste of money.
Quicken is excellent and have used it for 20 years
The updates haven't worked for years and I no longer use it, and in any case lost the computer it was on in a hurricane and have no access on my current computer.

I don’t like being forced to update the software to get the  functions that I already paid for and you can’t remove the notice to renew and activate. I’ve used Quicken since 2097 but am now considering Quickbooks since I’m told it is better.
I don't have anything bad to say about Quicken.  I love the product, and I love QuickBooks as well.
Reliable. Excellent features.I wish there was a Linux version, though, so I could stop using Windows entirely.
Used Q for years. Could never haver maintained the important historical record without it.
Your customer service person knowable, understanding and communication was easily to understand,

I've communicated this to Quicken personnel, but received no reply and nothing was ever done to remedy that problem.Despite that one issue, I still love the Quicken financial app and recommend it highly to anyone who wishes to stay on top of their transactional details.

The trick is to be able to do both - continue to enhance the system while maintaining the ease of use and consistency that the existing users have come to depend upon. Change isn't always "an improvement". Most users, no matter what the software, quickly find a straight line path that works best for them. Usually anything beyond that becomes an unwanted distraction. This conclusion is based upon over 30 years of developing accounting software.More troubling is that bugs reported (by me) are not addressed, there is no follow-up when they are reported, and at $100 / year for the home market, expectations are higher. Unfortunately there is very limited competition, which if it existed, would help create a more responsive situation and benefit the consumer greatly.  With that as the backdrop, it is still probably the best out there - but it is not what it could and should be.

I used to love Quicken.  Now I tolerate it... for now.  I don't like the change to an annual subscription model, but I can understand it.  And at least they promise that your data is always available to you if your subscription lapses.  And that's true-ish, but boy they make you jump through hoops to access it this year.  It's bad enough that they they hijack a big chunk of your screen real estate for the nag boxes (plural) telling you to renew--and naturally you can't close them.  But this year, wow.  Ridiculous hoops to jump through to use the program "manually" (i.e. without a subscription) and my experience was that you have to follow these steps (reinstalling the program and the latest allowable patch while disconnected from the internet, then reconnect so the program can phone home to verify... what, exactly?) each time you want to open the program or use a different data file.Did I contact customer support on this jump-hoops-multiple-times issue?  In fairness, no I didn't.  I could've given them a chance but I don't have any confidence in their tech support based on my prior experiences.  Occasionally I've had issues with data corruption, and after having me run the automatic validation/rebuild, their only advice is to open a good backup and truncate your data file so the current year is the only data.  If you want a yearly history of data, you can always open multiple data files, run the reports, and manually consolidate them.  That's a lot of work every time I want a history on some random item.  So instead of doing that I keep all my data in one file (which support recommended that I not do).  And if I find corruption I have a robust, versioned backup that lets me go back to before the corruption happened and then just re-enter all the new data.These days Quicken seems to be more focused on building and selling additional services rather than fixing a number of bugs that have been in the program for years.  And good luck trying to give them feedback.  The program lets you submit bug reports/feedback online, but there's never a response.  Some old bugs I've submitted multiple times--simple things--are still broken.  At least they seem to fix the things that crop in in new releases.  And unless you're contacting them about a specific, immediate issue, there's really no way to contact them.  No contact info on the web site other than for support  And the marketing emails have a reply-to address that looks like you can actually reply but it's a bounce instead.I used to love Quicken.  Now I tolerate it.  And I'm finally at the point where I'm evaluating alternatives and figuring out how to transfer a couple decades' worth of data over.  So you got one more year out of me while I figure out the best way to make this transition and then hopefully I'm done.  Quicken does a lot of things well but with all the drawbacks they've lost me.  Sadly there's zero way to tell them this unless they read this purchase feedback that's really their exit interview.

Quicken has been my go-to tool for personal finance management for years, helping me track spending, investments, and budgets. Unfortunately, my experience with the software in recent years has been riddled with frustrations, leading me to question whether it still delivers the value it promises. Here’s my take on where Quicken excels and, more importantly, where it falls short.1. An Outdated User Interface and ExperienceOne of the first things I noticed when using Quicken is how dated its interface feels. Navigating the software has become an exercise in patience. Tasks that should be straightforward, like reconciling accounts or creating a budget, often feel overly complicated. In comparison to modern apps like YNAB or Mint, Quicken feels clunky and unintuitive. For software I’ve used for so long, it’s disappointing to see how little effort has been made to modernize the user experience.2. Constant Failures with Financial Institution IntegrationThis is where Quicken has let me down the most. The ability to download transactions from my bank and credit card accounts has become unreliable at best, and unusable at worst. Transactions often fail to download entirely, duplicate entries appear without explanation, and I’ve even had to manually input data—completely defeating the purpose of using Quicken.Banks frequently change their connection methods, and Quicken seems unable to adapt quickly enough, leaving users like me to deal with the fallout. For software that markets itself as a comprehensive financial tool, this is a massive flaw that disrupts my ability to maintain accurate records.3. Ongoing Performance IssuesOver the years, I’ve encountered persistent performance problems with Quicken. Crashes, slow loading times, and glitches have become regular occurrences. These issues are especially frustrating when I’m working on time-sensitive tasks, like reconciling accounts at the end of the month. Each update seems to bring more problems than solutions, leaving me feeling like I’m constantly troubleshooting instead of managing my finances.4. High Cost, Limited ValueThe cost of Quicken’s subscription model is difficult to justify given these challenges. I’ve paid for features and functionality that consistently fall short. Compared to alternatives like Mint (which is free) or YNAB (a flat $99 per year), Quicken feels like a relic that charges premium prices without delivering premium value.5. A Lack of InnovationAs someone who has used Quicken for years, I can’t help but notice how little it has evolved. While competitors are integrating AI, automation, and more advanced investment tools, Quicken seems to have stalled. The lack of meaningful updates or forward-thinking features leaves me wondering if the company is even trying to keep up with the competition.6. A Frustrating Web-Only ExperienceIn today’s mobile-first world, I was disappointed to discover that Quicken doesn’t offer a dedicated mobile app. Instead, users are directed to a web browser experience, which feels clunky and incomplete. For me, this lack of a true mobile solution makes managing my finances on the go a hassle.The web browser interface isn’t optimized for mobile use, and performing even basic tasks like reviewing transactions or checking budgets often requires navigating tiny menus and awkward layouts. For a company that positions itself as a premium financial tool, the absence of a robust mobile app is a glaring oversight.7. Customer Support That Falls ShortWhen I’ve reached out to Quicken’s customer support, the experience has been anything but helpful. Long wait times and unproductive responses have made solving technical issues a chore. For software that charges an annual subscription fee, this lack of reliable support feels like adding insult to injury.Conclusion: My Take on Quicken TodayQuicken was once a powerful tool that I relied on for my financial management. But my recent experiences with the platform have left me frustrated and disappointed. Between the constant integration failures, performance issues, outdated design, and lack of meaningful innovation, it’s hard to justify the cost—or the time I spend trying to make it work.If Quicken wants to remain relevant, it needs to address these critical flaws and modernize. Until then, I’m seriously considering moving to a more reliable and user-friendly alternative.

I have been using Quicken for over 20 years to manage my finances.  Quicken used to be problem / bug-free when I used it in the early days.  Not so any more.  I frequently have problems with Quicken not doing what it is supposed to do.  Here are four examples:1.  When I enter new payments or income items as Reminders, and then go to the Reminder list and enter the Reminder I just established, Quicken will enter the transaction in the appropriate Register(s), but then it will remove the Reminder from the Reminder list, so that it is no longer visible in the Bill and Income Reminders list for that month, as a completed transaction.  This is intermittent.  It happens for many of my new transactions, but not all.  It is extremely aggravating, because there is no rhyme or reason to which Reminders it will remove and which it will leave in the Reminder list when they are entered as completed transactions.2. On several of my accounts for which I have transaction Registers, and for which I download transactions from the associated bank or other institution, into the Quicken Register for the account, I have had numerous missing transactions from downloads.  I have then had to do a great deal of time-consuming research and troubleshooting to restore the missing transactions to the relevant account Register, and to get Quicken to stop giving me incomplete transaction downloads for that institution.3. In the Register for one of my Investment accounts, there are numerous transactions that are for investments in a 401K account from my employer (a very large, well-known, long existent corporation).  These are typical proprietary funds for an employer 401K, not traded on the open markets like ETFs, mutual funds, and stocks available to everyone.  However, I have, in prior years, always been able to download transactions for these proprietary funds into the Register for my 401K account, and have them recognized by Quicken with the actual correct name of the investment fund / security.  Near the beginning of this year, Quicken started no longer recognizing these funds during downloads, as it downloaded additional shares from a fund or security already existing in my 401K account Register.  It wanted me to create a new name for the security, different than the name of the security already listed in the Holdings list for that Investment account, and in the overall Security List for all Investment accounts.  There was no other way to get Quicken to recognize these shares as from an "existing" Security (already in both of these lists).  I had to create a new name for the Security for these shares, to get them downloaded into my account Register for my 401K.  Needless to say, this has created a ton of new work for me now, to get this mess straightened out.  I will have to go back through hundreds of transactions individually, and edit them, to change the name of the Security in each of these transactions, to the correct existing / original Security name, in place of the "new" Security name I was forced to come up with during the transaction download.4. When I download transactions from a particular merchant, and fill in the details for the transaction (select an expense Category and fill in the Memo field), Quicken "remembers" these details, and automatically fills in this exact same information for all future downloaded transactions from that same merchant.  This is wreaking havoc with keeping all of my accounts at their correct balances, because sometimes these transactions involve a Category that is an Asset account that has its own Register and balance in Quicken.  I cannot find any way in Quicken to turn this "feature" off (automatically remembering and filling in transaction details for future transactions from the same merchant).These are just some of the most aggravating problems I have encountered recently in Quicken.

Quicken Premier for Mac is not much help if your intention is tracking investments. It's far inferior to Microsoft Money, and it's far inferior to Quicken for PC. Quicken for Mac does not easily allow for benchmarking, and it does not allow for calculating rates of return for customized date intervals. (It only allows rates of return calculations for year to date, one year, three year, and five year). If an investment is sold and the proceeds are automatically transferred into a brokerage account, seemingly unnecessary keystrokes are required (they're not required for Quicken for PC). It's a mystery to me why Quicken for PC and Quicken for Mac cannot be the same. TurboTax is the same whether using a PC or a Mac, why not Quicken? In conclusion, Quicken is the best financial software that I've found, but if you have a choice between the PC and the Mac version, buy the PC version.

I have been using Quicken since the '80s when it was called Checkfree and ran on DOS. Over the years it was improved as the underlying technologies advanced and eventually became part of the Intuit family. I seldom used the budgeting or online downloads from my banking institutions. I used the Bill Pay feature and the reporting functions. Bill Pay was reliable and easy to use. You would request a bill to be paid to a selected payee, you chose the amount and the date it was to be paid, and Quicken did the rest automatically. You didn't have to decide if it was a check payment or a direct bank transfer payment. Quicken paid the bills and the checks arrived on time.Then came Bill Manager. Last year Intuit changed the bill payment interface and subjected their users to a months-long beta test. I was on the phone numerous times to tech support (who always tried to be as helpful as they could) but many of the problems persisted. I have stopped using Quick Pay altogether (the direct transfer from my payment account to the payee) because of the intermittent failures. On the day the bill was to be paid I would get a "Failed (Quick Pay)" error message which naturally resulted in late payment fees and interest charges from my lender or credit card company. I still use Check Pay, but it seems to take much longer to deliver than it did under the previous Bill Pay software. I allow at least 10 days or more to send the check before the due date.Despite these frustrations, I'm vested in Quicken for the convenience of categorizing my expenses, generating reports at tax time, and having an accurate account of where my money is spent. The vast majority of the user interface was unchanged when Quicken abandoned Bill Pay and migrated to Bill Manager, so the user interface is still fairly Intuitive (pun intended) and easy to use. But too many quirks and problems remain with the software and I would not recommend it, in good conscience, to anyone else.

The conversion to Quicken Bill Manager in October 2022 has been nothing short of a disaster!I have been a faithful Quicken user since 1996 through good times and a few quirky times. Due to some issues apparently imposed by security concerns with interfacing to Bank of America, Quicken has changed its seamless bill payment methodology to something termed Quicken Bill Manager consisting of two fairly disparate functions called Quick Pay and Check Pay.Quick Pay claims to be able to send electronic payments to over a purported 11,000 payees who have online accounts accessible by Quicken.  Since October, I have been able use Quick Pay with only two of my well over 20 vendors.  Attempts to use Quick Pay with the remaining vendors result either in an interminable wait with a 'Fix It' button that does nothing, or an error message stating 'Quick Pay Error: Payment Account Declined'.  Apparently, some billers require that a new payment account first be validated before being used to pay a bill.  In each case, I followed Quicken's instructions to resolve this issue: I logged in to the biller’s website and initiated an Add Payment Account process.  With the exception of the two accounts referenced above, this has never worked.  Either I am doing something wrong and can find no direction on any Quicken support site or there is some flaw in the Quick Pay procedure.I have been able to make payments by turning to Check Pay, the facility whereby a check can be sent to anyone in the United States with an address through a Quicken service.  Unfortunately, only five Check Pay transactions are allowed without charge per month [nine during an introductory period] and then additional transaction much be purchased at a fee of three for $3.00.  Since I have essentially been unable to use Quick Pay and must use Check Pay for everything, this cost is becoming prohibitive.  This is especially frustrating since, prior to the change, I was required to pay nothing to either BoA or Quicken for any check processing.Other 'human factors' problems exist: there is no way to convert a Check Pay to a Quick Pay or vice versa; there is no way to edit a Quick Pay on the Bills & Income page; there is no way to copy and paste a previous payment transaction; and numerous other idiosyncrasies.  This whole package is definitely not ready for prime time.  I have wasted tens of hours simply trying to pay my bills on time utilizing what should be the heart and soul of a money management system.I am sad to say that this is the first time in over 25 years as a Quicken user that I am actively considering the acquisition of a different program.

Here is the text of my recent response to Eric Dunn, CEO of Quicken:EricFirst, thanks for this message.
